raw_response:
Well, let me sit down and think through this year's planning. I'm 49 now, been working these fields since I was 14, so I've seen plenty of good years and bad ones. My twelve mu isn't much but it's been feeding us for a long time.

**The main ground — wheat and maize (about 8 mu)**

Most of my land goes to wheat-maize, same as always. That's what everyone around here does and it gives us our grain and some to sell. I'll plant wheat around October 10th or so, after the maize comes off in early October. I use the variety my cousin got from the seed shop in town last year — Jimai something, can't remember the number, but it did okay for him so I'll try it too, maybe 10 yuan per mu for seed.

For fertilizer, I do what I've always done — about one bag of compound (15-15-15) per mu before I plow, that's around 40 kg, and then at the spring green-up when the wheat stands up again I'll topdress with urea, maybe half a bag per mu, so around 20-25 kg. If the wheat looks yellow I'll put on a little more, if it looks dark green I'll hold back. Two years ago I put on too much and it lodged in June with a bad wind — lost a lot. So I'm careful now.

I'll water the wheat maybe 3 times — once after planting to get it going, once at green-up, and once at booting. Water from my well costs me in diesel, about 15 yuan per mu each time, so I don't waste. If it rains good I skip one.

Maize goes in right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste, that week is always a rush. I use a hybrid seed, something like Zhengdan 958 or whatever the agent has, about 30 yuan per mu. Maize I don't fertilize as heavy — one bag of compound at planting and maybe one topdress of urea at the big-trumpet stage. Usually no irrigation if the summer rains come, but if July is dry I'll water once or twice.

**Stevia — about 2 mu**

I put in stevia on my 2 mu of sandier ground about three years ago when the village cooperative started buying it. It pays better than maize per mu if you can manage it. I transplant seedlings in April. It needs more care — weeding is hard work since we can't use the same herbicide as wheat, so my wife and I spend a lot of days bent over pulling weeds. Three harvests in a season. Fertilizer — I put down some organic manure from old Li's farm (he has pigs) plus one bag of compound per mu.

**Vegetables — the rest (about 2 mu)**

I grow a bit of cabbage, cauliflower, chili, and eggplant — maybe half a mu each. Mostly for the family to eat and my wife sells some at the market in town on Wednesdays. Cabbage and cauliflower are autumn crops, I'll transplant in August after the summer maize starts tasseling on that corner plot. Chili and eggplant go in May and produce all summer. These take more fertilizer and more watering but the pieces are small so it's manageable. I use more manure on the vegetable ground — keeps the soil good and saves money on chemical fertilizer.

**What worries me**

Money is tight. Three people in the household and my son works away — sends some home but we can't count on it. My wife helps me with everything. We don't hire labor except maybe at wheat harvest if the combine operator comes. Fertilizer prices went up again this year, I heard from old Zhang. So I'm not going to put on more than last year — can't afford it. I keep some cash back in case the well pump breaks or someone gets sick.
